theme: Subsurface Drainage Flow Modeling Research Gaps
description: This theme covers identified gaps and future research priorities in understanding and modeling water movement in subsurface drainage systems, including preferential flow characterization across varying soil and management conditions. theme: Future Research and Management Practices Needed
description: This theme addresses gaps in current knowledge and practice, emphasizing the need for further research to identify cost-effective nutrient mitigation strategies and improved cropping practices, while also highlighting alternative edge-of-field and agronomic approaches to reduce nutrient losses from tile-drained agricultural landscapes.

representative_3: If a similar risk of yield losses related to changes in N application amount and timing are observed, greater emphasis should be placed on other approaches such as cover crops and edge-of-field practices (e.g. bioreactors, wetlands, and buffers) to meet N load reduction targets in Illinois.

description: This theme covers research gaps and practical strategies for reducing nitrate-N losses to subsurface drainage water and groundwater. representative_3: Some potential management practices to reduce soil NO3-N and subsequent leachate and groundwater NO3-N concentrations include reducing N application during the first years after the initiation of irrigation, reducing N applications by having reasonable yield goals and giving proper credit for fall residual soil NO3-N, and adjusting N applications based on adverse weather conditions or poor soil properties that may affect crop growth.

description: This theme covers identified gaps and methodological recommendations for studying nutrient (N and P) losses and water balance in drained organic soils.
